title: Print Heading Tier Restyle Part Through Nested Paragraph
description:
In the print report, the sectioning/heading chip system (print/tex/semio-window.sty) needs a fully specified 14-level (plus frozen tail) visual hierarchy so every heading depth is unambiguously distinguishable by fill color, text emphasis, and (for the deepest levels) border weight:

1 Part - Tertiary fill (semio-tertiary), emphasized text
2 Chapter - Tertiary fill, normal gray text
3 Section - Secondary fill (semio-secondary), emphasized text
4 Subsection - Secondary fill, normal gray text
5 Subsubsection - Primary fill (semio-primary), emphasized text
6 Paragraph - Primary fill, normal gray text
7 Subparagraph - Normal fill (semio-chrome-panel), emphasized text
8 SubSubparagraph - Normal fill (semio-chrome-panel), normal gray text
9 SubSubSubparagraph - No fill, emphasized text, emphasized border (semio-chrome-border-emphasized)
10 SubSubSubSubparagraph - No fill, normal gray text, emphasized border
11 SubSubSubSubSubparagraph - No fill, emphasized text, normal border (semio-chrome-border-normal)
12 SubSubSubSubSubSubparagraph - No fill, normal gray text, normal border
13 SubSubSubSubSubSubSubparagraph - No fill, emphasized text, no border
14+ SubSubSubSubSubSubSubSubparagraph and deeper - No fill, normal gray text, no border (frozen forever, no further alternation)

Currently: chapter/section/subsection/subsubsection get colored chips (cycling semio-secondary/semio-tertiary/semio-secondary/semio-primary), part gets no chip at all (stock KOMA), paragraph falls into an undifferentiated gray "muted" fallback, subparagraph is completely untouched, and everything deeper via the custom SemioNest recursive nesting mechanism renders identically to paragraph with no per-depth distinction.

Implementation plan (all changes in print/tex/semio-window.sty, within existing %region Headings and %region NestedParagraphs):
1. Generalize \semio@koma@heading@lines to take a text-color parameter (currently hardcodes semio-chrome-foreground in two call sites) and thread it through \semio@heading@lines@dispatch and the \chapterlinesformat override.
2. Replace the single \semio@heading@color@* table in \semio@heading@installall with a paired fill+text table covering part, chapter, section, subsection, subsubsection, paragraph, subparagraph per the table above. This moves paragraph off \semio@koma@heading@lines@muted onto the colored path - that macro's only real caller disappears; remove it once confirmed unused (do NOT touch \semio@window@header@muted/\semio@heading@cap@muted/\semio@heading@cap@muted@tab, which is the unrelated window/figure/table title-chip system).
3. Wire \part into the chip system: add a \partlinesformat override mirroring the existing \ifcsname chapterlinesformat\endcsname guard pattern used for chapter (verify \partlinesformat's exact arity against real KOMA behavior via a test compile; fall back to a direct \part override if it doesn't exist/match).
4. Wire \subparagraph: verify whether stock \subparagraph already flows through \sectionlinesformat (in which case the table registration in step 2 plus a \setkomafont{subparagraph}{...} suffices) or needs a bespoke wrapper reusing \semio@heading@pair/\semio@heading@chip.
5. Add subparagraph to \semio@heading@install@spacing's call list.
6. SubSubparagraph (row 8) = SemioNest depth 1, uses the panel fill tier (reuse the same accent-chip machinery with semio-chrome-panel as the "accent" color) - not the no-fill painter.
7. For SemioNest depths >= 2 (rows 9-14+): build a new parametrized "no-fill" painter (plain-TeX/\ifcsname conditional idiom matching the rest of the file, no expl3) taking a text color and a border-color-or-empty, painting only border rules with no fill rectangle. Replace the fixed \ifcase depth-styling with a depth-to-(text,border) lookup table per the row table above, clamping depth >= 7 to row 14's style so it freezes forever (matches "repeat last for deeper" spec).
8. Note: the existing SemioNest counter chain (semio@nest@a..@e) only supports depth 1-5 today (numbering silently stops incrementing past depth 5) - this is a pre-existing latent bug distinct from styling; only fix the visual styling per depth in this ticket, flag the numbering limitation as known if not addressed.
9. Remove now-dead paragraph-specific muted painter primitives once confirmed unused elsewhere.

Verification: find the print build/verify command (print/project.json nx targets -> bun ./script.ts build, run via nx per CLAUDE.md), build a fixture .tex exercising \part through \subparagraph then SemioNest nested 7+ levels deep in both light and dark theme, rasterize and visually confirm fill/text/border per level and that depth 8+ freezes pixel-identical. Confirm TOC/list entries still register for Part and Paragraph (dispatch path changes). Confirm no regression to the unrelated window/figure/table title-chip muted rendering.
summary:
Third pass: fixed a sizing/positioning bug in the outline (no-fill, bordered) chip variant reported by the user — the bottom border line was floating partway inside the chip instead of sitting flush at the bottom edge, unlike the solid chips.

Root cause: \semio@heading@cap@nofill@vbox's bordered branch stacked [top-stroke hbox][content hbox][bottom-stroke hbox] inside a \vbox to \semio@chrome@titlebar@height, but the content hbox (\hbox to \semio@window@cap@w{\hfil\usebox{...}\hfil}) only forced its WIDTH, not its height — it kept its natural (small, text-only) height. With no stretchable glue anywhere in the three stacked items, the \vbox's "to <height>" just registers a bigger box without redistributing the shortfall, so the bottom stroke rendered right after the text rather than at the box's true bottom edge (the solid-chip pattern avoids this because \semio@window@cap@paint already wraps its content in a \vbox to <forced-height>{\vfil...\vfil}).

Fix: added \semio@window@cap@paint@nofill (a fill-less mirror of \semio@window@cap@paint, same \vbox to <height>{\vfil...\vfil} centering, just without the \rlap fill rectangle) and used it in \semio@heading@cap@nofill@vbox's bordered branch with explicit height \dimexpr\semio@window@cap@body@h-\semio@stroke@hairline\relax — matching the exact geometry the solid/muted chip variants already used.

Verified: rebuilt the verify-refined-hierarchy.tex fixture (all 9 levels + 3 SemioNest depths) — the "Underfull \vbox" warnings that were present in every previous build (silently signaling this exact bug) are now gone, and the rasterized PDF shows every outline chip's border flush with the top/bottom edges, identical sizing to the solid chips. Ran the full `bun print:test` suite afterward (12 PDFs, all templates x both themes) with no regressions.
